$comment: GENERATED FILE — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Produced by `pnpm env:python-surface` from the services' pydantic-settings declarations plus an AST scan of non-pydantic reads. `pnpm env:python-surface --check` fails when it is stale; `pnpm env:sync` consumes it to generate every apps/<svc>/.env.sample, turbo.json#globalEnv and the docs table.

fields.name: GUARDRAIL_CONFIG_CACHE_TTL_S
fields.description: TTL (seconds) for the resolved per-tenant config cache (OQ2 ~60s).

fields.name: GUARDRAIL_DATABASE_URL
fields.description: Read-only connection string to the shared HOPE core DB.

fields.name: GUARDRAIL_V2_QUEUE_MAX_CONCURRENT
fields.description: Concurrent async analyse jobs — the ONLY field here with a reader (`main.py`). Lived on the deleted engine sub-config (`settings.engine.max_concurrent`), which made a queue bound look like an engine knob; it is the job queue's own limit. The wait/retry/backoff/batch quartet that sat alongside it had no reader at all. admission waiting is `transport.max_queue_wait_s`, which IS read.

fields.name: GUARDRAIL_REDIS_URL
fields.description: The alias is not decoration. `env_prefix="GUARDRAIL_REDIS_"` + a field named `redis_url` resolves to `GUARDRAIL_REDIS_REDIS_URL` — a stuttering name nothing sets. Every operator-facing file says `GUARDRAIL_REDIS_URL` (`.gitlab/ci/test.yml:695` even wires it to `$CI_REDIS_URL`), so the documented name has never actually reached this service and CI has been silently testing against the localhost default. Found by the Python drift gate; the stuttering form stays accepted so nothing that DID set it breaks.

fields.name: GUARDRAIL_PORT
fields.description: `GUARDRAIL_PORT` is the fleet-wide name for this concept: it is what `scripts/dev-service.sh:267` passes to uvicorn, what `.env.test` sets to 8963, and what `apps/api/src/__tests__/env-port-standardization.test.ts` pairs with `GUARDRAIL_URL`. Only `GUARDRAIL_V2_PORT` was ever readable here, so every one of those declarations reached the launcher and not the app — harmless while uvicorn always wins, and wrong the moment anything reads `settings.port`. Accept both; the fleet name first.

fields.name: GUARDRAIL_SERVICE_TOKEN
fields.description: Inter-service authentication. The gateway provisions this under the canonical GUARDRAIL_SERVICE_TOKEN key (turbo.json / .env.example), so read it verbatim via validation_alias — NOT the GUARDRAIL_V2_ env_prefix, which never matched the gateway and left prod enforcement silently disabled.

fields.name: GUARDRAIL_V2_GATEWAY_URL
fields.description: Where the control plane lives (env GUARDRAIL_V2_GATEWAY_URL). This is BOOTSTRAP TRANSPORT (the address of the config source), NOT config authority: the retention knobs themselves come from the effective-config route this URL points at.

fields.name: GUARDRAIL_V2_HOST
fields.description: Application

fields.name: GUARDRAIL_V2_OTEL_ENABLED
fields.description: Observability

fields.name: INTERNAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
fields.description: CANONICAL internal credential (owner decision D-D, 2026-08-17) ONE shared access token for ALL internal service-to-service communication, identical across every HOPE service, set by the DevOps engineer, internal use only. Unprefixed on purpose (`validation_alias` bypasses the env_prefix) — it belongs to no single service. This is what the service ACCEPTS inbound as `X-Service-Token` and PRESENTS on every outbound peer call. The legacy per-service token below stays accepted / used as a zero-cost backward-compatibility fallback; both empty ⇒ auth bypassed (dev / CI).

fields.name: NLP_URL
fields.description: Where `apps/nlp` lives — guardrail's classification/NER executor after BOOTSTRAP TRANSPORT (an address), not config authority: read from the repo-wide `NLP_URL`, so guardrail adds no env var of its own.

fields.name: TEXT_URL
fields.description: Where `apps/text` lives. BOOTSTRAP TRANSPORT (an address), not config authority — read from the repo-wide `TEXT_URL`, so guardrail adds no env var of its own.

fields.name: HARNESS_CLAIM_CHECK_BUCKET
fields.description: Tenant-scoped, access-controlled PHI bucket (NOT a public bucket).

fields.name: HARNESS_CLAIM_CHECK_ENABLED
fields.description: Offload ON by default (protect the history budget); the threshold keeps small payloads inline so tiny prompts/notes never pay a store round-trip.

fields.name: HARNESS_CLAIM_CHECK_ENDPOINT_URL
fields.description: Self-hosted MinIO S3 endpoint (host under platform control — no cloud egress).

fields.name: HARNESS_CLAIM_CHECK_MIN_BYTES
fields.description: Blobs at/above this many utf-8 BYTES are offloaded; below it they stay inline.

fields.name: HARNESS_CLAIM_CHECK_STORE
fields.description: Backend selector: ``memory`` (process-local fake — dev/test) | ``s3`` (self-hosted MinIO).

fields.name: MINIO_CERT_CHECK
fields.description: `validation_alias` deliberately ESCAPES the `HARNESS_CLAIM_CHECK_` prefix: this is one platform-wide trust decision about one object store, and it is the same bare variable apps/stt reads and `turbo.json#globalEnv` declares. A `HARNESS_CLAIM_CHECK_CERT_CHECK` of its own would be a second knob that can disagree with the first about a single fact. `AliasChoices` and not a bare `validation_alias`: the alias REPLACES the field name for init as well as for env lookup, so `ClaimCheckConfig( cert_check=...)` (tests, and any direct construction) would be rejected as an extra field. Listing both keeps the platform variable authoritative and the field constructible by name.

fields.name: HARNESS_EVAL_CASE_CONCURRENCY
fields.description: How many golden-set cases GoldenSetRunner scores concurrently. ``1`` (default) is the original strictly-sequential behaviour — safe for any backend, including a single-slot local server. CI raises this (see ``HARNESS_EVAL_CASE_CONCURRENCY`` in ``harness-eval-gate``) to match the judge service container's parallel slot count; actual in-flight network concurrency to the judge endpoint is still bounded by the separate ``HARNESS_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENCY`` governor (``harness.core.llm_concurrency``), so raising this alone can never burst past what the endpoint allows.

fields.name: HARNESS_EVAL_GOLDEN_SET_VERSION
fields.description: Pinned golden-set version the gate runs against (CI overrides via env).

fields.name: HARNESS_EVAL_ICC_GATE_ENABLED
fields.description: Whether the judge↔clinician ICC calibration check gates the run at all. Default True (unchanged behaviour for every existing caller/test). A small non-reasoning CI judge can be prone to a ceiling effect — scoring every quality dimension near-identically across cases — which drives ICC(2,1) to ~0 regardless of whether its underlying agreement (Gwet AC2, computed and reported alongside it) is actually strong; `icc_threshold` is validated to [0, 1] (see `_unit_interval` below), so a near-zero-but-technically-negative ICC reading from that ceiling effect can never be recalibrated into passing by lowering the threshold alone. CI sets `HARNESS_EVAL_ICC_GATE_ENABLED=false` for its specific small judge rather than silently widening `icc_threshold` outside its valid range or forcing a pass on a statistic that is structurally uninformative for that model — see harness-eval-gate's env-var comment in `.gitlab/ci/test.yml` for the measured numbers.

fields.name: HARNESS_EVAL_ICC_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Release-gate thresholds. OWNER RULING 2026-08-20: lowered 0.80 -> 0.73 to the MEASURED baseline (icc=0.7306, Gwet AC2=0.9196, n=288, golden set curated-v2.0.0, reproduced 2026-08-18). This is a recorded baseline, not a target: the shortfall against the 0.80 literature bar is accepted as debt. Restore 0.80 once a clinician-authored golden set or a higher-dynamic-range judge is available. Do not raise this value without re-measuring; do not lower it further without a new owner ruling.

fields.name: HARNESS_EVAL_MAX_CASES_PER_RUN
fields.description: Hard cap on cases the SYNCHRONOUS internal ``/eval/run`` endpoint will score in one request (apps/api promotion gate + admin run-now). Larger sets belong on the future Temporal lane; the endpoint rejects an over-cap request (413) rather than blocking a promotion for minutes.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_ANCHORED
fields.description: Calibration levers Opt-in anchored rubric prompt: appends rubric-faithful per-score guidance + balanced exemplars so a small local judge applies the Epic grade descriptors consistently (raises judge↔reference agreement). The verbatim instrument is preserved; this is purely additive. Default off to keep CI prompts pristine.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_ENTAILMENT_BATCH_SIZE
fields.description: Groundedness batching: claims verified per judge call. ``1`` keeps the legacy one-call-per-claim path byte-for-byte; ``>= 2`` states the shared transcript premise ONCE and labels that many claims in a single JSON-array call (``ceil(N / size)`` long-prefill calls instead of N), the dominant latency lever for the inferential pass. Conservative parser: any ambiguous array item degrades to ungrounded, so a larger batch can never loosen a verdict.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS
fields.description: Large budget (NOT ~2k): reasoning model families (qwen3.5, gemma-4, medgemma) can spend thousands of tokens "thinking" before emitting the JSON answer; a small cap truncates mid-reasoning (finish_reason=length → empty ``content``, the answer stranded in ``reasoning_content``). 8192 leaves room for the reasoning trace *and* the final JSON across both reasoning/non-reasoning models.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_OUTPUT_MODE
fields.description: Judge output format: "with_explanation" (default; richer per-dimension rationale) or "score" (compact score-only JSON). SCORE is markedly more reliable for small (≤~7B) judge models, which can otherwise emit a long un-tagged prose preamble that exhausts ``max_tokens`` before any JSON appears.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_PROVIDER
fields.description: Priority/default = a small ≤20B model on a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. gemma-4-e2b-it-qat is the owner-standardized default (2026-08-16): the one model resident in LM Studio, verified served by the live dev instance.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_SC_TEMPERATURE
fields.description: Temperature used for the >1 self-consistency samples (needs > 0 for diversity). Kept low (0.2) so samples stay near the greedy mode while still varying enough for the per-dimension median to reduce variance without drifting off-rubric.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_SEED
fields.description: Deterministic decoding seed (passed to OpenAI-compatible / Azure backends).

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_SELF_CONSISTENCY
fields.description: Self-consistency: sample the judge ``self_consistency`` times and take the per-dimension median (variance reduction). ``1`` == single deterministic pass.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_TIMEOUT_S
fields.description: Generous default: a slow local reasoning judge can take minutes for a single call (observed ~90s on gemma-4-e4b, ~340s on qwen3.5-9b via LM Studio), so the old 120s default killed legitimate calls mid-generation.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_TRANSIENT_RETRIES
fields.description: Bounded app-level retry for *transient* backend failures (distinct from the SDK's ``max_retries``, which does NOT retry HTTP 400s). A small local server (e.g. LM Studio serving gemma-4-e4b) can terminate/unload the model engine under sustained sequential load — surfacing as ``400 {'error':'terminated'}`` or a dropped connection — then JIT-reload it on the next call. We retry such transient failures (with linear backoff to let the model reload) so a long run survives a mid-run engine crash; a genuinely-down backend still aborts once the retries are exhausted (never a silent green gate).

fields.name: HARNESS_MCP_MAX_ATTEMPTS
fields.description: Bounded transport retries inside the client for a transient/5xx error before the activity degrades (never crashes the loop).

fields.name: HARNESS_MCP_MAX_RESULT_BYTES
fields.description: Result size cap (utf-8 BYTES). A tool result above this is claim-checked (offloaded, keeping the blob OUT of Temporal history) when claim-check is enabled, else truncated to the cap. Mirrors the claim-check threshold.

fields.name: HARNESS_MCP_TIMEOUT_S
fields.description: Per-call wall-clock timeout for a single MCP tool invocation.

fields.name: HARNESS_JUDGE_OPENAI_COMPAT_JSON_RESPONSE_FORMAT
fields.description: ``response_format.type`` sent on json_mode calls (claim extraction / verify). "json_object" works on Ollama/vLLM; LM Studio rejects it ("must be json_schema or text") and small models emit empty output under a strict json_schema grammar, so set this to "text" for LM Studio to omit the constraint and rely on the "Return ONLY JSON" prompt + tolerant parsing (harness.eval.jsonio.loads_json).

fields.name: HARNESS_RETRIEVAL_COLLECTION
fields.description: The PLATFORM's collection. A tenant that brings its own Qdrant may prefix it from its own connection row (`extraJson.collection`, the console's "Collection prefix"); the derivation lives in ONE place (`provider_credentials.apply_vector_credential`) so ingest, retrieval and delete can never disagree about which collection a tenant's vectors are in.

fields.name: HARNESS_RETRIEVAL_EMBEDDINGS_BASE_URL
fields.description: `embeddings_model` and `embeddings_dim` are ONE coupled description: the dim MUST match the loaded model AND the Qdrant collection. They nevertheless live in DIFFERENT tiers, and the split is deliberate — the model is a SELECTION and resolves from the connection row (tenant → platform); the dim is a property of the Qdrant collection, which no connection row can declare, so it stays here. A row that pins a different-dimension model gets a Qdrant dimension rejection (visible, degrade-safe) rather than silently wrong vectors. Keep them adjacent.

fields.name: HARNESS_RETRIEVAL_EMBEDDINGS_DIM
fields.description: Dense vector dimension — MUST match the loaded model AND the Qdrant collection, which is why it did NOT follow the model onto the connection row: the dim describes the COLLECTION as much as the model, and a connection row has nowhere to declare one. It therefore stays an env-tier sizing knob. A row that pins a different-dimension model gets a Qdrant dimension rejection — visible and degrade-safe — which is the same outcome the field comment above already promised for a tenant BYO model.

fields.name: HARNESS_RETRIEVAL_ENABLED
fields.description: The landmine A.2 cited is still live and still worth heeding: a KEYLESS row injects on NEITHER tier. That is now a DEFINED outcome (`absent` ⇒ call the endpoint unauthenticated) rather than a silent no-op.

fields.name: HARNESS_RETRIEVAL_RERANKER_BASE_URL
fields.description: HF Text-Embeddings-Inference reranker root (cross-encoder ``/rerank``).

fields.name: HARNESS_RETRIEVAL_TOP_K_RETRIEVAL
fields.description: Hybrid knobs: dense+sparse prefetch limit -> RRF fusion -> cross-encoder rerank.

fields.name: HARNESS_SENSOR_ATOMIC_FACT_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Reference-free atomic-fact verifier: >= 80% of the note's atomic claims must be entailed by the transcript per the DETERMINISTIC self-hosted NLI (a second, model-cheap groundedness gate alongside the LLM-judge groundedness sensor). Regen-fixable; a degraded backend degrades (never auto-PASS).

fields.name: HARNESS_SENSOR_CITATION_PRESENCE_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Every provenance claim must carry >= 1 evidence span.

fields.name: HARNESS_SENSOR_CITATION_VERIFY_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Inferential (institutional RAG): >= 80% of CITED claims must be entailed by their cited knowledge chunk(s) per the same judge — a strict citations check (regen-fixable; degrades to the "unverified" badge on outage).

fields.name: HARNESS_SENSOR_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD
fields.description: >= 80% of transcript entities must be reflected in the note.

fields.name: HARNESS_SENSOR_ENTITY_FAITHFULNESS_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Zero-tolerance: any note entity ungrounded in the transcript fails.

fields.name: HARNESS_SENSOR_GROUNDEDNESS_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Inferential: >= 80% of provenance claims must be entailed by the transcript/evidence per the LM Studio judge (lower than the zero-tolerance checks — semantic entailment is graded, not exact-match).

fields.name: HARNESS_SENSOR_NUMERIC_DOSE_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Zero-tolerance: every numeric/dose value in the note must match the transcript.

fields.name: HARNESS_API_INTERNAL_PREFIX
fields.description: apps/api internal-harness mount. ``HarnessInternalController`` sits under the global ``/api/v1`` prefix (``@Controller('internal/harness')``), so the live, out-of-the-box mount is ``/api/v1/internal/harness``. Override via ``HARNESS_API_INTERNAL_PREFIX`` if the gateway prefix ever changes.

fields.name: HARNESS_ATOMIC_FACT_ENTAIL_THRESHOLD
fields.description: Per-claim entailment decision: P(entailed) >= this ⇒ grounded.

fields.name: HARNESS_ATOMIC_FACT_MODEL_CACHE_DIR
fields.description: Cache dir for weights materialised from an `s3://` source_uri.

fields.name: HARNESS_ATOMIC_FACT_MODEL_PATH
fields.description: Optional self-hosted MiniCheck-Flan-T5 GGUF entailer (owner directive 2026-07-11: "GGUF everywhere"). When `atomic_fact_model_path` is set (a staged local .gguf), the verifier swaps the model-free DeterministicOverlapEntailer for the MiniCheck NLI; unset (default) keeps the hermetic model-free entailer. `model_id`/ `model_file` are provenance only. A build/calibration failure falls back to the safe deterministic entailer (see `_atomic_fact_entailer`). CPU-default (Q6 quant). BOOTSTRAP FALLBACK ONLY. The runtime value comes from the control plane's effective-config `modelWeights['minicheck-flan-t5-large']` (harness holds no DB handle, so it cannot read the control plane directly). This env var applies when that key is absent — which is every deployment until the `modelWeights` control-plane rollout completes — so behaviour predating that rollout is preserved byte-for-byte.

fields.name: HARNESS_ATOMIC_FACT_N_CTX
fields.description: 512 matches Flan-T5's training context (`n_ctx_train`); MiniCheck windows long documents to ~512-token chunks, so more only wastes the encoder KV alloc and trips llama.cpp's `n_ctx_seq > n_ctx_train` overflow warning.

fields.name: HARNESS_CONSENT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
fields.description: TTL for `ConsentClient`'s per-(tenant, patient, purpose) cache — a bounded-staleness BACKSTOP, not the propagation mechanism (mirrors `.claude/rules/09-infrastructure-devops.md` §Config caches rule 2; this phase has no cross-process invalidation channel for the harness worker, a disclosed, TTL-bounded scope choice — see consent-design.md). Mirrors the TS-side ConsultationConsentService cache TTL (30s).

fields.name: HARNESS_CONSENT_INTERNAL_PREFIX
fields.description: Gateway-internal consent-assert mount. A SIBLING of api_internal_prefix (``ConsentInternalController`` is `@Controller('internal/consent')`, not nested under `internal/harness`), so it gets its own prefix rather than reusing the harness one.

fields.name: HARNESS_ENVIRONMENT
fields.description: Deployment signal. Deliberately SEPARATE from ``debug``: that flag defaults False, so "not debug" cannot distinguish a production deploy from unconfigured local dev — and the claim-check guard below must not fire on the latter. Production/staging deploys set ``HARNESS_ENVIRONMENT`` explicitly.

fields.name: HARNESS_GUARDRAIL_BASE_URL
fields.description: Peer service — the summarization palette's `guardrail.check` node calls apps/guardrail directly, mirroring the established `text_base_url`/`nlp_base_url` bootstrap floor pattern (rule 09 §Configuration Tiers: a `*_URL` transport address is the ONE sanctioned kind of hardcoded default). `X-Tenant-Id` is mandatory on every call.

fields.name: HARNESS_HOST
fields.description: Application

fields.name: HARNESS_INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN
fields.description: Dedicated token for the institutional-knowledge ingest endpoint (``POST /internal/knowledge/ingest``). The ingest guard accepts an ``X-Service-Token`` matching THIS secret OR the shared ``service_token``; empty (and an empty shared token) disables the guard for local dev. The BullMQ ingest processor presents this as the ingest contract's token.

fields.name: HARNESS_MAX_CONCURRENT_ACTIVITIES
fields.description: F-29 — Worker-level admission cap (``Worker(max_concurrent_activities=...)``, ``worker.py``). Left unset, Temporal admits activities unbounded, which lets many concurrent inferential activities queue behind the single ``HARNESS_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENCY`` semaphore (``core/llm_concurrency.py``) — a cheap non-LLM activity (fetch_policy, persist_entities, ...) can then starve behind that queue. Kept deliberately conservative (well above ``HARNESS_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENCY``'s default of 1, since most admitted activities never touch the LLM governor at all); raise together with ``HARNESS_LLM_MAX_CONCURRENCY`` if the semaphore is ever raised.

fields.name: HARNESS_MAX_REGEN
fields.description: Bounded-regen budget + clinician-gate timing (durable, deterministic).

fields.name: HARNESS_MODEL_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
fields.description: BOOTSTRAP FALLBACK ONLY — the runtime value comes from the control plane (`harness.modelCache.{ttlSeconds,maxModels}`), applied by `sensors.inferential.minicheck_entailer.configure_entailer_cache`. Env: HARNESS_MODEL_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS / HARNESS_MODEL_CACHE_MAX_MODELS. The 600 s default is an owner decision; maxModels 1 preserves today's residency exactly.

fields.name: HARNESS_OPTIMISTIC_DELIVERY_ENABLED
fields.description: Optimistic two-phase delivery kill-switch. The FIRST key of the two-key optimistic gate; the second is the durable ``workflow.patched`` marker (permanent in code). Read here, in NON-workflow settings, and snapshotted into ``HarnessGateConfig`` at workflow start (document:start + the policy merge), so it stays deterministic across replay — never read from env inside the workflow body. Default OFF ⇒ the legacy single-phase path, byte-identical to before optimistic delivery.

fields.name: HARNESS_OTEL_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT
fields.description: Precedence matches STT and the OTel collector: DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT (what the k8s overlays patch) then NODE_ENV (the repo-wide selector, ) then "development".

fields.name: HARNESS_OTEL_ENABLED
fields.description: Default OFF and requires an explicit endpoint (not just the flag) — a bare ``HARNESS_OTEL_ENABLED=true`` with no collector configured must not change startup behaviour. See ``otel_tracing_enabled`` below.

fields.name: HARNESS_PROMPT_SIZE_WARN_CHARS
fields.description: F-19 — assembled-prompt size alarm (``HARNESS_PROMPT_SIZE_WARN_CHARS``). The doc loop deliberately re-sends the ENTIRE template+transcript prefix on every regen iteration and never compacts or truncates it: dropping clinical content to fit a budget is the wrong failure mode. This threshold makes an oversized prompt VISIBLE instead — above it the ``generate`` activity emits a structured ``harness.prompt_size_warn`` and generates anyway. 400_000 chars ~= 100k tokens at the chars/4 heuristic, i.e. the point where a long consultation starts to crowd a 128k-context model.

fields.name: HARNESS_REDIS_URL
fields.description: ENV-TIER and staying that way: this is how the process REACHES Redis, which is exactly the bootstrap floor rule 09 reserves for env — a value delivered over the channel it configures could never bootstrap itself. Unreachable ⇒ the service still boots and still converges on the TTL backstop.

fields.name: HARNESS_SERVICE_TOKEN
fields.description: LEGACY per-service credential (empty = auth disabled for local dev). This is HARNESS_SERVICE_TOKEN: it guards the inbound internal endpoints AND is the ``X-Service-Token`` the api_client presents to apps/api when the shared INTERNAL_ACCESS_TOKEN above is unset.

fields.name: HARNESS_TEMPORAL_METRICS_HOST
fields.description: Loopback by default: this is a PHI-processing service and must not become LAN-reachable by accident. `scripts/dev-service.sh` takes the same posture for the HTTP ports; containers override with 0.0.0.0.

fields.name: HARNESS_TEXT_BASE_URL
fields.description: Loop / gate-adapter Tool-service base URLs the durable loop calls out to.

fields.name: HARNESS_TEXT_PROVIDER
fields.description: Text generation defaults (None => let the Text service choose).

fields.name: HARNESS_TEXT_TIMEOUT_S
fields.description: There are deliberately NO `HARNESS_ACTIVITY_START_TO_CLOSE_S`, `HARNESS_ACTIVITY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` or `HARNESS_GENERATE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` knobs. They were declared here, advertised in `.env.sample` and `turbo.json`, and read by NOTHING: Temporal activity timeouts and retry policies are module-level constants in `temporal/workflows.py` (`_INFERENTIAL_TIMEOUT`, `_INFERENTIAL_RETRY`, `_GENERATE_RETRY`) and MUST be, because a workflow body may not read env — that is the determinism rule 06 states. Wiring them would break replay; the honest fix is that they are gone. `test_task799_dead_settings.py` keeps them gone.

fields.name: INTERNAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
fields.description: CANONICAL internal credential (owner decision D-D, 2026-08-17) ONE shared access token for ALL internal service-to-service communication, identical across every HOPE service, set by the DevOps engineer, internal use only. Unprefixed on purpose (`validation_alias` bypasses the env_prefix) — it belongs to no single service. This is what the service ACCEPTS inbound as `X-Service-Token` and PRESENTS on every outbound peer call. The legacy per-service token below stays accepted / used as a zero-cost backward-compatibility fallback; both empty ⇒ auth bypassed (dev / CI).

fields.name: TEMPORAL_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S
fields.description: Grace period the worker gives in-flight activities to finish (or observe cancellation) after shutdown is requested, before it force-cancels them. 0 = cancel immediately (Temporal's default). Applies on SIGINT/SIGTERM.

fields.name: NLP_EXTERNAL_TEXT_MAX_RETRIES
fields.description: Bounded retry for a transient blip, mirroring `ExternalGuardrailConfig`: total tries = max_retries + 1, linear backoff.

fields.name: TEXT_URL
fields.description: `TEXT_URL` is the repo-wide name for this address — `apps/guardrail` already reads it under the same alias, and `turbo.json#globalEnv` declares it once for the whole fleet. `NLP_EXTERNAL_TEXT_BASE_URL` was a second name for the same endpoint: two names for one address is how half a fleet ends up pointed at a decommissioned host.

fields.name: MEDICAL_SUGGESTER_USE_GPU
fields.description: Performance settings

fields.name: API_GATEWAY_KEY
fields.description: Internal service authentication key presented as X-Internal-Service-Key on gateway /internal/* calls.

fields.name: HF_HOME
fields.description: Unprefixed (`validation_alias` bypasses the `NLP_` prefix) because it belongs to the huggingface stack, not to this service. It arrives through the ONE canonical loader — `hope_env.load_env()` at the top of this module — and is pushed back into `os.environ` by `apply_hf_home` below. Empty = the huggingface default.

fields.name: INTERNAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
fields.description: CANONICAL internal credential (owner decision D-D, 2026-08-17) ONE shared access token for ALL internal service-to-service communication, identical across every HOPE service, set by the DevOps engineer, internal use only. Unprefixed on purpose (`validation_alias` bypasses the env_prefix) — it belongs to no single service. This is what the service ACCEPTS inbound as `X-Service-Token` and PRESENTS on every outbound peer call. It is the ONLY accepted credential on this service — the legacy per-service `NLP_SERVICE_TOKEN` was REMOVED (see the note below), so a peer that presents anything else is answered 401. Empty ⇒ auth bypassed (dev / CI). Guardrail presents this same value via `peer_service_token()`.

fields.name: NLP_GATEWAY_URL
fields.description: Where the control plane lives (env NLP_GATEWAY_URL). This is BOOTSTRAP TRANSPORT (the address of the config source), NOT config authority: the service-level knobs themselves come from the effective-config route this URL points at.

fields.name: NLP_INFERENCE_BATCH_MAX_SIZE
fields.description: `inference_batch_linger_ms` is the ENTIRE latency price of batching: an otherwise-idle request waits at most this long for company. Keep it well under the p50 forward pass, or batching costs more than it saves.

fields.name: NLP_INFERENCE_DEVICE
fields.description: TRANSPORT/TOPOLOGY, not model identity — env-tier for the same reason the batch geometry is, and unlike a model id, which may never be a settings default. "cpu" is the bootstrap floor because it is the only placement that is correct on every host; "auto" degrades to the best device present; an explicit "mps"/"cuda" that is absent RAISES rather than silently running 3x slower on CPU (see `nlp.core.device`).

fields.name: NLP_INFERENCE_DEVICE_CPU_ONLY_MODULES
fields.description: Submodules kept on CPU when the device is an accelerator. This is a runtime-COMPATIBILITY fact about the installed `gliner2`/torch build, not policy: `count_embed.gru` trips an MPSNDArray assertion that ABORTS the process (SIGABRT, not an exception), so the relocation is mandatory wherever that build is used. A torch release that fixes it is answered by emptying this list, not by editing code.

fields.name: NLP_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENT
fields.description: Bootstrap fallback; the runtime value comes from the control plane (`nlp.inference.maxConcurrent`).

fields.name: NLP_INFERENCE_MAX_INFLIGHT_BATCHES
fields.description: Concurrent forward passes against ONE model. Small on purpose: torch already parallelises inside a pass, so stacking passes on the same weights buys cache contention rather than throughput.

fields.name: NLP_INFERENCE_QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH
fields.description: The queue is bounded so overload degrades into a 503 instead of an OOM.

fields.name: NLP_LOG_LEVEL
fields.description: Typed `int` (a `logging` level number) but written by operators as a NAME — `apps/nlp/.env.sample` shipped `LOG_LEVEL=info`, and every other service in the fleet takes a name. So `NLP_LOG_LEVEL=INFO` used to be a boot-time ValidationError while `NLP_LOG_LEVEL=20` was undocumented anywhere. Accept both spellings of the ONE name ; `core/logging.py` reads the same variable and resolves it the same way.

fields.name: NLP_METRICS_ENABLED
fields.description: Reads NLP_METRICS_ENABLED first (the fleet convention — every other service uses its own prefixed switch: TEXT_METRICS_ENABLED, TTS_METRICS_ENABLED, GUARDRAIL_V2_METRICS_ENABLED, HARNESS_METRICS_ENABLED, METRICS_ENABLED for STT). It used to read ONLY the gateway-scoped OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED, which .env.dev sets to false — so NLP's /metrics was disabled by a variable documented under the API gateway. OTEL_METRICS_ENABLED is kept as a fallback for compatibility.

fields.name: NLP_MODEL_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS
fields.description: BOOTSTRAP FALLBACK ONLY — the runtime value comes from the control plane (`nlp.modelCache.{ttlSeconds,maxModels}`). Env: NLP_MODEL_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS / NLP_MODEL_CACHE_MAX_MODELS.

fields.name: NLP_OTEL_ENABLED
fields.description: Master switch: gates traces, metrics, AND log export (default off).

fields.name: NLP_PEER_CALL_MAX_CONCURRENT
fields.description: Owner decision (2026-08-20): outbound peer HTTP (the `nlp` → `text` delegation behind `/classify/topic`/`/classify/intent`) gets its OWN bound, never `inference_max_concurrent`. That semaphore protects local GPU/CPU inference slots; a slow HTTP round-trip to `text` is a completely different resource (this process's own outbound connection/concurrency budget) and must not be able to starve — or be starved by — local classification. Bootstrap fallback only; the runtime value comes from the control plane (`nlp.peerCall.maxConcurrent`), configured the exact same way as `inference_max_concurrent` above.

fields.name: NLP_REDIS_URL
fields.description: It exists so the `arca:config:invalidate` subscriber built in `core/effective_config.py` has a transport. Before D-5 this service held no Redis client at all, so that channel had a handler and no wire, and every control-plane write took a full TTL window to be seen here. The TTL stays as the bounded-staleness backstop (rule 09 §"Config caches"), so a process that boots while Redis is down still starts and still converges.

fields.name: NLP_SERVICE_NAME
fields.description: Declaring the alias instead puts every one of them back on the shared chain: init > host env > secrets_dir > .env.<NODE_ENV> > default. The prefixed `NLP_*` name is listed FIRST so `turbo.json#globalEnv`'s declaration is the reachable one; the unprefixed / OTel-standard names the deployment already sets stay accepted behind it.

fields.name: NLP_TORCH_NUM_INTEROP_THREADS
fields.description: `0` = auto, which is ONE inter-op thread: this service runs sequential encoder forward passes, so a second pool adds no parallelism and contends for the same quota.

fields.name: NLP_TORCH_NUM_THREADS
fields.description: `0` = auto, and auto reads the CONTAINER's CFS quota (`hope_env.cpu.effective_cpu_quota`) — never `os.cpu_count()`, which reports the NODE. On `hope-nlp` that difference was 2 vs 48 and cost a measured 11.7x on BERT-base FFN shapes, with the pod spending 7,292 s frozen on the quota against 573 s executing (TASK-892 §2.2). Read by `nlp.torch_runtime.configure_torch_threading`, which runs from `nlp/__init__.py` before any torch import.

fields.name: NLP_WARM_MODELS
fields.description: A SCHEDULING lever, never a selection one: a request still names its own model, resolved tenant-first by the caller, and an entry here only decides that those weights are loaded before the first caller asks. The control-plane set (`warmModels`) is loaded too and WINS on a duplicate; this exists only because nothing produces that key today, which left the warm path inert while a cold `/guard/*` call was being cancelled and restarted forever (TASK-930 D-7). Retire it once `warmModels` is served.

fields.name: SECURITY_CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS
fields.description: Credentialed CORS is OFF by default. `apps/nlp` is an internal service reached by the gateway and by peer services, never by a browser carrying a session — so it has nothing to gain from credentialed cross-origin requests, and everything to lose from `*` + credentials.

fields.name: TEXT_CLASSIFIER_USE_GPU
fields.description: Performance settings

fields.name: TOKEN_CLASSIFIER_USE_GPU
fields.description: Performance settings

fields.name: API_GATEWAY_KEY
fields.description: Internal service authentication key

fields.name: API_GATEWAY_URL
fields.description: Internal API Gateway URL

fields.name: APP_NAME__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: The prefixed name is listed FIRST so it wins, and the bare name stays accepted so existing deployments keep working. Fields that name genuinely SHARED infrastructure — `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `MINIO_*` — are deliberately left bare: one address, one value, every service. BUILD IDENTITY, not configuration — and therefore not settable from env (rule 09 §Release Versioning: build identity "must never be made settable from a Deployment manifest, an env file, or `turbo.json#globalEnv`"). The authoritative version is the release tag baked into the image's `build-info.json`, which `hope_env.BuildInfoReader` reads; these two are only the in-process labels used before that file is consulted. They were bare fields, so `APP_VERSION=9.9.9` in the shared env file would have made this service report a version nobody built — the exact defect that had `apps/api` reporting `0.1.0` in every deployed environment.

fields.name: AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT
fields.description: Default Azure storage account name (used when STORAGE_PROVIDER=azure_blob).

fields.name: AZURE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_KEY
fields.description: Default Azure storage account shared key.

fields.name: AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING
fields.description: Default Azure connection string (preferred over account/key when set).

fields.name: AZURE_STORAGE_ENDPOINT_SUFFIX
fields.description: Default Azure storage endpoint suffix.

fields.name: CORS_ORIGINS
fields.description: CORS — EMPTY by default. stt handles PHI audio, and the browser never talks to :8861 directly (the gateway fronts every route), so there is no origin this service can name for itself. `["*"]` was the shipped default; an operator with a genuine direct-browser need sets CORS_ORIGINS explicitly rather than inheriting a wildcard nobody chose.

fields.name: DATABASE_ENABLED
fields.description: Open the read-only Postgres connection (deprecated paths only; TASK-861).

fields.name: DATABASE_URL
fields.description: PostgreSQL connection string (read-only access)

fields.name: DIARIZATION_DEVICE__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Device for pyannote inference (auto, cuda, cpu)

fields.name: HUGGINGFACE_CACHE_DIR
fields.description: HuggingFace model cache directory

fields.name: INTERNAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
fields.description: Shared internal service access token accepted as X-Service-Token.

fields.name: METRICS_ENABLED
fields.description: Enable Prometheus metrics on /metrics

fields.name: MINIO_ACCESS_KEY
fields.description: EMPTY defaults, not `minio_admin`. A credential is never a literal in code (rule 00 §Configuration Principles), and a WORKING default is the worse half of that rule: it silently masks a failure to load the real one, so the first environment where the compiled-in credential does not happen to be valid is the first place anyone finds out. Both are registered `vault-kv` platform secrets (`minio.accessKey` / `minio.secretKey` in `platform-secrets.descriptors.ts`) and reach this process either through the Vault Agent `secrets_dir` tier or `.env.dev`.

fields.name: MINIO_CERT_CHECK
fields.description: ⚠️ DELIBERATE, REVERSIBLE SECURITY RELAXATION (owner ruling 2026-08-30, `MINIO_CERT_CHECK`). Defaults to False — TLS certificates are NOT verified. That is a statement about how this platform is deployed today, not about what is safe: there is no private CA, MinIO serves HTTPS on :9000 with a certificate nothing here can chain to a trusted root, and MinIO authenticates with a service account (access key + secret) rather than the certificate. Defaulting to "verify" would fail every object-store call closed. PHI hardening is explicitly de-prioritised for now; when a CA lands, set `MINIO_CERT_CHECK=true` (or flip this default) — grep `MINIO_CERT_CHECK` for every consumer, in this service and in apps/api / apps/harness.

fields.name: MINIO_ENDPOINT
fields.description: MinIO (Object storage)

fields.name: MODEL_CACHE_MAX_MODELS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Maximum number of models in LRU cache. Bootstrap fallback — the runtime value comes from the control plane (effective-config).

fields.name: MODEL_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Idle TTL for cached models in seconds (product clamp: min 60s / max 3600s). Active sessions pin models so TTL applies only after the last release. Bootstrap fallback — the runtime value comes from the control plane (effective-config); the clamp is re-applied to whatever is served.

fields.name: ONNX_NUM_THREADS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Number of threads for ONNX Runtime intra_op parallelism. 0 = auto (recommended): ONNX Runtime auto-sizes to physical CPU core count with proper thread affinity. Set explicitly only if profiling shows benefit.

fields.name: OTEL_ENABLED
fields.description: Enable OpenTelemetry distributed tracing

fields.name: OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT
fields.description: OTLP gRPC collector endpoint

fields.name: PARAKEET_CPP_LIBRARY_PATH__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Path to libparakeet shared library (env PARAKEET_CPP_LIBRARY_PATH)

fields.name: PARAKEET_CPP_NUM_THREADS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: CPU threads for parakeet.cpp inference

fields.name: PUBSUB_CHANNEL_PREFIX__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Redis Pub/Sub channel prefix for real-time transcription events. Full channel: {prefix}{job_id}. The NestJS subscriber listens on the same channel to relay events via SSE.

fields.name: PUBSUB_ENABLED__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Enable Redis Pub/Sub publishing for real-time transcription events. When disabled, the worker skips event publishing but still calls the gateway API for job lifecycle updates.

fields.name: PUNCTUATION_DEVICE__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Device for punctuation inference: 'cpu', 'cuda', 'auto'

fields.name: PUNCTUATION_MAX_LENGTH__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Max sequence length / sliding window width for punctuation model

fields.name: PUNCTUATION_MODEL_CACHE_DIR__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Cache dir for punctuation model weights (None = HF default cache)

fields.name: REDIS_URL
fields.description: Redis connection string for Dramatiq

fields.name: SEGMENT_MERGE_GAP_THRESHOLD_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Maximum gap (seconds) between adjacent VAD speech segments that allows merging into a single inference chunk.  Merging reduces the number of Whisper generate() calls, each of which incurs ~6s encoder overhead on CPU.  Default 2.0s works well for conversational audio with natural pauses.  Set to 0 to disable merging entirely.

fields.name: STORAGE_PROVIDER__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Default object-storage provider when no per-tenant storage descriptor is supplied. The default keeps using the global MinIO client unless set to 'azure_blob'. Set it on the platform storage row, not in env — STORAGE_PROVIDER no longer reaches this field.

fields.name: STREAMING_AUDIO_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Seconds of no audio data before STT auto-stops a streaming session (default 5 min).

fields.name: STREAMING_AUDIO_STREAM_MAXLEN__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Approximate MAXLEN for Redis audio streams (per-session). The SINGLE source of truth for the audio-stream bound: kept equal to the TS gateway bridge's XADD MAXLEN (the sole production writer of stt:audio). At ~30-80ms/frame this retains minutes of audio, comfortably ahead of the consumer group.

fields.name: STREAMING_AUDIO_TRIM_INTERVAL_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Minimum interval (seconds) between XTRIM MINID calls on the consumed portion of stt:audio:{session_id}. 0 disables consumed-portion trimming (MAXLEN bound still applies).

fields.name: STREAMING_EXTRA_FILLER_PATTERNS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Pipe-separated extra regex alternates appended to the streaming hallucination filler pattern. Default empty — built-in English + Malayalam filler forms only.

fields.name: STREAMING_INFERENCE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Max seconds finalize waits for the inference queue to drain before building the transcript. On timeout (e.g. GPU backlog) the still-queued tail utterances are transcribed inline rather than dropped, so the last utterance is never lost.

fields.name: STREAMING_INFERENCE_QUEUE_MAXSIZE__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Bound on the per-session in-process inference queue (SessionManager._register_inference_runtime). F-08: the steady-state enqueue is a bounded wait_for (not a blocking put) — once the queue is full for longer than the bounded wait, the utterance is DROPPED (with a structured warning + counter) rather than blocking the single ingestion dispatch loop, which would otherwise stop XACK'ing Redis audio frames and let stt:audio's MAXLEN trim unread raw audio. The finalize-path drain uses the separate streaming_inference_drain_timeout_s bound and is unaffected.

fields.name: STREAMING_INFERENCE_STOP_TIMEOUT_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Seconds to wait for a session's inference worker task to drain/stop before giving up (used both on graceful session removal and when force-finalizing on session-end).

fields.name: STREAMING_MAX_AUDIO_BUFFER_BYTES__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Hard cap (bytes) on the in-memory audio buffer per session. Once exceeded, new frames are silently dropped and a warning is logged. Default ~500 MB ≈ ~87 min of 16 kHz mono s16le audio.

fields.name: STREAMING_MAX_BATCH_SIZE__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Maximum batch size for the dynamic batch scheduler (GPU inference). 0 = auto-detect from ExecutionProfile based on hardware.

fields.name: STREAMING_MAX_CONCURRENT__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Maximum number of concurrent streaming sessions. 0 = auto-detect from ExecutionProfile based on hardware. Bootstrap fallback — the runtime value comes from the control plane (effective-config), applied after hardware detection.

fields.name: STREAMING_PUNCTUATION_TIMEOUT_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Max seconds a streaming FINAL waits for Cadence-Fast punctuation before the raw text is published (0.3-0.5 s recommended). Applies only when the punctuation model resolves to 'cadence-fast'.

fields.name: STREAMING_REAPER_INTERVAL_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Interval (seconds) between background reaper scans for expired sessions.

fields.name: STREAMING_RESULT_STREAM_EXPIRE_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: TTL (seconds) for Redis stream keys after session closes (1 hour).

fields.name: STREAMING_RESULT_STREAM_MAXLEN__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Approximate MAXLEN for the per-session Redis result stream (stt:result). Bounds the stream DURING an active session (previously unbounded until the post-close EXPIRE). High enough that a keeping-up bridge/consumer never misses a result; overflowed finals remain in the durable transcript.

fields.name: STREAMING_SESSION_METADATA_EXPIRE_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: TTL (seconds) for Redis session metadata keys after session closes (24 hours).

fields.name: STREAMING_SESSION_PERSIST_INTERVAL_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: How often (seconds) to persist session metadata to Redis.

fields.name: STREAMING_SESSION_TIMEOUT_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Seconds of inactivity before a streaming session is auto-finalized by the reaper.

fields.name: STREAMING_SNAPSHOT_INTERVAL_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Interval (seconds) between audio snapshot uploads to S3 during active streaming sessions.

fields.name: STREAMING_TRANSCRIPT_OUTBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Max re-drive attempts for a transcript in the durable Redis outbox before it is dropped with a loud alert. When the inline persist exhausts its retries on a TRANSIENT error the transcript is enqueued to a shared Redis outbox and re-driven by the reaper loop (any worker) with an idempotency key; a PERMANENT (4xx) error is dropped immediately rather than retried.

fields.name: STREAMING_TRANSCRIPT_PERSIST_BACKOFF_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Base backoff (seconds) between durable-transcript persist retries; the delay scales with the attempt number. 0 disables the wait (used in tests).

fields.name: STREAMING_TRANSCRIPT_PERSIST_MAX_ATTEMPTS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Max attempts to persist the durable streaming transcript to the gateway during finalize. The transcript is the clinical system of record AND the harness auto-draft trigger, so a transient gateway blip is retried rather than silently swallowed. The persist endpoint is idempotent, so retries never double-create the transcript or re-trigger the harness. Must be >= 1.

fields.name: STREAMING_WORKER_HEARTBEAT_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Interval (seconds) between worker heartbeat extensions in Redis.

fields.name: STREAMING_WORKER_HEARTBEAT_TTL_S__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: TTL (seconds) for the worker heartbeat key in Redis.

fields.name: STT_MODEL_S3_SECURE
fields.description: Use TLS for a BARE host:port s3:// model endpoint (set false for local MinIO). A URL-form endpoint — the platform-storage fallback's http://… — decides for itself.

fields.name: STT_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME
fields.description: Service name in traces and metrics

fields.name: TORCH_NUM_INTEROP_THREADS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Number of threads for PyTorch inter-op parallelism (torch.set_num_interop_threads). Default 1 is optimal for single-request inference. Increase only for concurrent batch processing.

fields.name: TORCH_NUM_THREADS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Number of threads for PyTorch intra-op parallelism (torch.set_num_threads). 0 = auto: uses the number of physical CPU cores. In K8s, set this to match the CPU request/limit (e.g. 8 for 8-core pods) to avoid under- or over-subscribing.

fields.name: TRANSCRIPTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Maximum transcription job timeout in seconds (default: 10 min)

fields.name: VAD_MIN_SILENCE_DURATION_MS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Minimum silence to end speech segment in ms

fields.name: VAD_MIN_SPEECH_DURATION_MS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Minimum speech segment length in ms (100 so short clinical confirmations survive)

fields.name: VAD_THRESHOLD__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Silero VAD speech detection threshold (0.0–1.0)

fields.name: WHISPER_CPP_NUM_THREADS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: CPU threads for whisper.cpp inference

fields.name: WORKER_MAX_RETRIES__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Maximum job retry attempts

fields.name: WORKER_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Dramatiq consumer poll interval max-backoff in milliseconds

fields.name: WORKER_THREADS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Number of Dramatiq worker threads per process

fields.name: TEXT_GATEWAY_URL
fields.description: bootstrap transport Where the control plane lives. This is the ADDRESS of the config source, not config authority: everything the route serves is itself control-plane owned. Env var: TEXT_GATEWAY_URL.

fields.name: TEXT_OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT
fields.description: Env var: TEXT_OTEL_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT. The presence of a collector address IS the enable signal, so there is no separate `TEXT_OTEL_ENABLED` that can disagree with it — and the default is EMPTY, i.e. no export, matching the `TEXT_OTEL_ENABLED=false` default it replaces. A default address would turn export on everywhere and make every process that has no collector spend its startup retrying one.

fields.name: TEXT_PORT
fields.description: process identity

fields.name: TEXT_REDIS_URL
fields.description: Env var: TEXT_REDIS_URL. Task state + the config-invalidation channel.

fields.name: TTS_KOKORO_DEVICE__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: No `voice` field: `af_heart` is already the catalog's kokoro binding for `en-female-1`, and the router supplies it as `req.provider_voice`. The warm-up path takes its voice from the catalog too (see `main.create_app`), so the string exists in exactly one place.

fields.name: API_GATEWAY_KEY
fields.description: Internal service authentication key presented as X-Internal-Service-Key on gateway /internal/* calls.

fields.name: INTERNAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
fields.description: CANONICAL internal credential (owner decision D-D, 2026-08-17) ONE shared access token for ALL internal service-to-service communication, identical across every HOPE service, set by the DevOps engineer, internal use only. Unprefixed on purpose (`validation_alias` bypasses the env_prefix) — it belongs to no single service. This is what the service ACCEPTS inbound as `X-Service-Token` and PRESENTS on every outbound peer call. The legacy per-service token below stays accepted / used as a zero-cost backward-compatibility fallback; both empty ⇒ auth bypassed (dev / CI).

fields.name: TTS_GATEWAY_URL
fields.description: Where the control plane lives (env TTS_GATEWAY_URL). BOOTSTRAP TRANSPORT (the address of the config source), NOT config authority.

fields.name: TTS_HOST
fields.description: Application

fields.name: TTS_MAX_INPUT_CHARS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Synthesis limits / defaults — control-plane owned.

fields.name: TTS_MODEL_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Idle TTL for local engine weights. BOOTSTRAP FALLBACK — the runtime value comes from the control plane (`tts.modelCache.ttlSeconds`), consumed via `core/effective_config.py`. Its env path is now CLOSED: it was documented as "BOOTSTRAP FALLBACK ONLY" while remaining fully settable, so an operator could set a value that the next config pull silently replaced.

fields.name: TTS_OTEL_DEPLOYMENT_ENVIRONMENT
fields.description: Resolved from the environment, defaulting to DEVELOPMENT. Copied "production" from the TEXT reference, which was itself the origin of this defect fleet-wide. A hardcoded "production" tags a developer laptop's spans as production data — a mislabelled dev span is noise, a mislabelled prod span corrupts an audit trail.

fields.name: TTS_OTEL_ENABLED
fields.description: Observability. Default OFF (never require a reachable collector to boot/serve). `otel_exporter_endpoint` defaults to empty (no hardcoded localhost target) so tracing activates ONLY when BOTH `otel_enabled` AND an endpoint are explicitly set — see `main.create_app`. TTS receives clinical text to synthesise, so `core/observability.py` wires a PHI-redaction hook into every span.

fields.name: TTS_REDIS_URL
fields.description: This does NOT make tts stateful. The connection subscribes to one pub/sub channel and evicts a cache; it reads no keys, writes none, and holds no tenant state. `apps/tts` stays the "genuine stateless, gateway-injected service" the assessment records — adding Redis for invalidation must never become a route to local tenant resolution.

fields.name: TTS_WARMUP_ENABLED__MOVED_TO_CONTROL_PLANE
fields.description: Local engines are LAZY by default: they register at boot but load their weights on the first synth request and are TTL-evicted when idle. Set TTS_WARMUP_ENABLED=true to restore boot-warm behaviour (fail-at-boot rather than first-request 503) — see docs/operations/inference/model-retention.md.
